problem.title: Edge count forcing a cycle in a connected graph
problem.informal_statement:
Show that a connected finite simple graph with at least as many edges as vertices must contain a cycle.

The target is stated for every such graph, with no bound on the number of vertices.

target_claim.statement: For every finite simple connected graph G = (V, E) with |E| >= |V|, G contains a cycle.

assumption_claims.statement: A cycle in a graph is a closed walk of length at least three whose vertices are pairwise distinct except for the coinciding endpoints.
Every finite connected acyclic graph on |V| vertices has exactly |V| - 1 edges.

formalization.statement: forall G : SimpleGraph, Finite(G) and Connected(G) and edges(G) >= vertices(G) implies exists c, IsCycle(G, c)
quantifiers: forall G a finite simple connected graph

definition_mapping: c is a closed walk of length at least three with pairwise distinct interior vertices
cardinality of the edge set E
cardinality of the vertex set V
assumption_delta: The informal statement says 'at least as many edges as vertices'; the formalization writes |E| >= |V| and adds no further hypothesis.
edge_case_delta: The empty graph is excluded by connectedness, which the formalization states explicitly.
Multigraphs and loops are excluded by simplicity, so a doubled edge does not count as a cycle here.

success_criteria: a derivation covering every finite simple connected graph, not a finite sample
stopping_rules: stop when the open obligation set is unchanged across two review points
